analysis: Reviewed landing/package-lock.json head lines 2368-3920, a lockfile-only change in the landing site's dependency tree. The patch bumps next 16.2.6 to 16.4.1 and sharp 0.34.5 to 0.35.5 with libvips 1.3.4, and updates postcss, nanoid and related optional platform packages. The visible head units show registry.npmjs.org resolved URLs and sha512 integrity values on every entry; no git, http or file sources, no tarballs from other hosts, and no removed integrity fields. The entries I could read are internally consistent: next 16.4.1 pins @next/env and the @next/swc-* packages at 16.4.1, the nested postcss is 8.5.23, sharp is optional and engines-bounded, and the ranges look coherent. The landing page is a marketing site outside the provider, coordinator and native-runtime scope. It touches none of the threat-model assets (A-001..A-018), trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009..TB-012) or threats. The lockfile is not in the provider artifact, attestation, App Attest or fan-helper path, so there is no regression against the T-034, T-013 or T-009 controls. Coverage limits: I could not see the patch for lines outside these units, so I did not check the integrity hashes of the sharp and libvips platform packages (lines 586-1370, outside the head text supplied) against the registry. I also could not verify that the upstream 16.4.1 and 0.35.5 releases are legitimate; that would need npm provenance and audit checks in CI. Nothing in the supplied evidence shows a malicious or tampered dependency. The only residual item is routine supply-chain hygiene, and I raise no finding.
